static_traits.name: Li Li
static_traits.family_status: Has a supportive spouse, enjoys spending time with family and friends; has the support of close friends
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; no psychotherapy or counseling received
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly and logically; able to self-reflect; fairly cooperative; marked tendency toward self-blame; low mood

basic_info.main_problem: After losing my passport while traveling, I felt irresponsible, which led to self-blame and feelings of incompetence.
basic_info.core_demands: The passport incident triggered a series of negative self-thoughts, affecting my self-esteem and well-being, prompting me to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: During a trip lasting several weeks, the client lost their passport amid managing multiple tasks, haste, and stress; after the incident, the client frequently blamed themselves, considering themselves 'irresponsible', and this feeling intensified when recalling the incident or planning future trips, together with worry about making mistakes again.

In the past, in situations such as organizing family activities and managing deadlines, the client repeatedly performed responsibly and handled things properly, but under the influence of the current event, these positive performances are ignored or treated as 'not counting'.

core_beliefs: I am incompetent / not competent enough

special_situations.event: Recalling the incident of losing a passport while traveling
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I lose important documents, it proves I am essentially irresponsible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Alerting oneself through constant self-reproach to avoid making mistakes again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too irresponsible, this mistake shows I am just this kind of person

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot fully control all the details, I will make mistakes again and prove I am irresponsible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying more thorough preparation and repeated checking to gain a sense of control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may lose things again, and the trip will spiral out of control again

special_situations.event: Needing to manage multiple tasks at once while traveling and feeling out of control
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel out of control in complex situations, it means I am not competent enough and cannot handle stressful matters
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tending to attribute loss of control to one's own flaws, and maintaining vigilance through self-criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am incompetent, I handle things badly

special_situations.event: Thinking of one's many responsible behaviors in the past
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One major mistake will cancel out all past positive performance
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negates positive evidence, focusing attention on this mistake to avoid carelessness
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The things I was responsible for do not count; I am still irresponsible

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as reliable and competent and to regain self-esteem and a sense of control
core_conflict.fear: Fears making another mistake and being labeled 'irresponsible', losing others' trust and further deprecating the self
defense_goal: Reduces the likelihood of making another mistake through self-harshness and increased control, in order to maintain a sense of safety and self-worth

object_relations.self_representation: A self-blamer who is wrongly defined and needs to prove oneself
object_relations.object_representation: Supportive and tolerant others (such as spouse, family, and friends)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing the lost passport incident in counseling or talking about future travel arrangements
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Regards a single mistake as a character flaw, believing they must bear responsibility for all consequences (transference: internalizing possible external evaluations as self-reproach)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes their own mistakes in a self-blaming tone, using absolute words (such as 'it is all my fault' and 'I am just irresponsible'), reducing the proportion of discussion of situational factors.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites them to recall past responsible behavior, or offers an alternative perspective
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes positive examples are insufficient to offset this mistake, tending to regard this event as decisive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses expressions such as 'this situation is special' and 'those do not prove anything' to downplay positive evidence, continuing to emphasize the seriousness of the event.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When emotions are strong, being asked to view events more objectively
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Keeps distance from emotions in an abstract, logical manner (such as 'I rationally understand the reasoning, but still feel it will not work')
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expounds cause-and-effect and logic in analytical language, with a steady tone but low emotional engagement, acknowledging 'knowing' but finding it hard to 'feel' it.

manifestations: Feeling out of control while traveling, longing for complete control to avoid mistakes
Views a single mistake as a permanent judgment on one's sense of responsibility
Worrying that mistakes will happen again in the future, trying to offset uncertainty with perfect preparation
outcomes: Significant stress when planning a future trip

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently uses self-deprecating labels ('I am irresponsible')
Hard to maintain self-compassion; tends toward harsh self-judgment
When discussing alternative perspectives, still excessively scrutinizes own mistakes and focuses on faults

exception_events.target_problem: When recalling losing the passport or planning future trips, the client usually falls into self-blame and low self-esteem, finding it hard to view events from a balanced perspective, resulting in obstructed travel plans.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In situations of organizing family activities or managing deadlines, the client can effectively coordinate and fulfill responsibilities, and the events are completed smoothly; this contrasts with the narrative of viewing themselves as 'generally irresponsible'.
exception_events.reason: Different support: support from a spouse, relatives, and friends; different context: tasks were clear and the pace was controllable; different understanding: focusing attention on concrete steps and execution, thereby gaining a sense of control and positive feedback.

positive_force: Having a supportive spouse and close friends, able to obtain emotional and practical support
In the past, performed responsibly in organizing family activities and managing deadlines, with effective planning and execution abilities
Possesses rational reflection ability, able to realize that 'one mistake does not define the whole self'
Willing to seek professional help and try concrete strategies to restore a sense of control
negative_force: Self-labeling and overgeneralization, tending to define one mistake as a character flaw
Worry about making another mistake leads to anticipatory anxiety
Persistent self-reproach and discounting of positive evidence
Feeling out of control in multitasking and high-pressure situations, increasing the negative cognitive cycle

antecedent: Recalling the incident of losing the passport
Feeling out of control under multitasking pressure
target_behavior.core_reason: Against a background of stress, overgeneralizes a single mistake into a stable personality defect, and maintains vigilance through self-reproach for fear of recurrence
target_behavior.function: Gains a sense of control and prevents further mistakes through self-criticism (escaping uncertainty and the feeling of being out of control)
target_behavior.consequence: Self-esteem declines, mood is low, anxiety increases, affecting future travel planning and daily life arrangements
